/assign @mrhohn @robscott

@RyanAoh It seems like there must be some kind of mistake here. If I'm understanding this PR correctly, it appears that `IPMode` was added as a required field without a default value, which would be a backwards incompatible change. Did you mean to add the new field as optional?

/cc @aojea @thockin

`IPMode` is an optional field. Looks like we should allow the load-balancer status updated with only ingress.ip specified, and the ingress.ipMode will default to "VIP" eventually.
The fllowing validation may need to be removed：
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4457f85eb3dfa34e46d6d776a3b7e89088dc9279/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L7066-L7069
Any advice? @thockin

> The following validation may need to be removed.

- remove the validation 
- default to "VIP"

Either can solve the failure without the e2e test change.
The failed CI can be fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119486. (Not related to this PR)

/retest

Should this be merged in v1.28? If yes, we need to tag the milestone v1.28.

/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-ubuntu-gce-network-policies
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-ipvs
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-ingress

> Thanks!
> 
> /lgtm /approve

/hold

I'm not sure this is correct, @thockin does this mean that old clients will not work once this feature is enabled if they don't set the field?

> I'm not sure this is correct, @thockin does this mean that old clients will not work once this feature is enabled if they don't set the field?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go#L146-L156

There is a logic to default IPMode to VIP for LoadBalancer when FG is enabled.

The problem with tests is that they don't run thru the WHOLE API stack, so default values are not set.  We get away with it a lot, but then you hit something like this and you need to go touch all of the test cases.  This is why pkg/api/service/testing/ exists, but we still have to convert everything to use it (and we have to deal with versioned vs unversioned)
LGTM label has been added.  <details>Git tree hash: eeb69491030c1800174742d83282591a98165558</details>

> The problem with tests is that they don't run thru the WHOLE API stack, so default values are not set.

This is an e2e test, this runs thru the whole API stack

The validation

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4457f85eb3dfa34e46d6d776a3b7e89088dc9279/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L7066-L7069

The defaulting and test

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go#L146-L156

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fdb2a07f8c4433db98a5e6247640221663bcc42/pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults_test.go#L1246-L1259

~~@aojea It sounds like that we should add a defaulting logic for service status. Right? I opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119674 to do a test. ~~ Need look into the code tommorrow.
Antonio is right. I skipped that this is E2E. It should be defaulted.

The defaulting logic is only for `LoadBalancer`.

But the e2e is using a `ClusterIP`.

See the code linked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119454#issuecomment-1657179394.

I think this is the root cause. I updated the PR.

/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-ubuntu-gce-network-policies
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-ipvs
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-ingress

Ahh.  The fact that we allow `ip` to be set when it's not a load-balancer is unfortunate.  I think the defaulting should change, so it sets `ipMode` whenever `ip` is set.

Hold on.  I see this code in pkg/registry/core/service/strategy.go: `dropTypeDependentFields()`:

```
    // Clear the load-balancer status if it is no longer appropriate.  Although
    // LB de-provisioning is actually asynchronous, we don't need to expose the
    // user to that complexity.
    if newSvc.Spec.Type != api.ServiceTypeLoadBalancer {
        newSvc.Status.LoadBalancer = api.LoadBalancerStatus{}
    }
```

Yet I just manually added an IP to a clusterIP service:

```
$ k get svc iamyouare -oyaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2023-01-17T17:55:27Z"
  labels:
    app: iamyouare
    foo: bar2
  name: iamyouare
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "35550324"
  uid: 1787eb65-4d45-4ad7-856c-73fbeb274a3f
spec:
  clusterIP: 10.0.168.22
  clusterIPs:
  - 10.0.168.22
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - name: p1
    port: 9376
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 9376
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP
status:
  loadBalancer:
    ingress:
    - ip: 1.2.3.4
```

Why is that not being wiped?

Ugh, spec vs. status.

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)

/lgtm

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119700 for followup

+1 for `Warn and then discard the value`. It seems to be a more API-consistent change.

/approve
